subject: Emerald Pay — token-thrash and 5xx wave after v4alpha quant deploy
messages:
From: Emily Chen <ops@emerald-pay.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: support@emerald-pay.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Degraded p99 + 5xx wave after v4alpha qprofile swap (urgent)

Avery —

We started seeing a sharp jump in p99 latency and a steady stream of 5xx errors starting ~08:50 PST after your team rolled the v4alpha qprofile to our production pool. Impact summary:

- p50: +10% (expected)
- p95: +28% (trending bad)
- p99: +220% (from ~480ms to ~1.6s)
- Error rate: 0.1% -> 1.9% (5xx and decode timeouts)
- Throughput: sustained tail drop during bursts (30% request failures under 200 rps bursts)

We attached the perf_trace_1109.json and profile_snapshot_1109.tgz. Logs show long decode stalls with token-level retries on hot paths; some requests are timing out at the gateway. This started immediately after the quant swap you announced Friday evening.

We're receiving angry PM/ops pings and the CTO is asking for an immediate remediation plan. Can you confirm rollback to the previous qprofile and open a priority incident? We need a timeline: rollback ETA, short-term mitigation (route to compatible model variant), and a plan for a postmortem.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Chen
Head of Production Ops
Emerald Pay
attachments: perf_trace_1109.json (application/json, 2.1MB), profile_snapshot_1109.tgz (tar.gz, 9.8MB)
From: avery_johnson@redwood.com
To: Emily Chen <ops@emerald-pay.com>, support@emerald-pay.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Degraded p99 + 5xx wave after v4alpha qprofile swap (urgent)

Emily —

Thanks for the heads-up and the traces. I see the same token-thrash pattern in the attached trace: long tail latencies concentrated on requests hitting hot-prefix caches after quant changes. I'm escalating this now to our on-call infra and the model ops team. Initial action plan:

1) Immediate: roll traffic off the v4alpha qprofile to the stable v4beta variant for the affected route(s). This is our quickest mitigation. (I will request the roll immediately.)
2) Short-term: enable strict prefix caching for bursty endpoints + bind to the older kernel selection to avoid the new kernel-path that appears to amplify stalls.
3) Investigation: full trace analysis, KV cache hit-rate delta, and a prioritized list of failing request ids (we'll share).

ETA for step 1 (traffic switch): 25 minutes from now, contingent on capacity.

Marissa / Jonas — I am looping you in for runbook execution and exec escalation if rollback is slower than ETA. Emily, I'll update you within 20 minutes with progress and the rollback ticket id.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Emily Chen <ops@emerald-pay.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Degraded p99 + 5xx wave after v4alpha qprofile swap (urgent)

Team —

On-call infra confirmed the behavior and we've executed a partial traffic steering to the v4beta variant for the primary inference pool. Observations so far: p99 started decreasing within 6 minutes of the steer, error rate dropping back toward baseline, but a subset of long-lived requests continue to surface decode retries.

Immediate notes and asks:
- Action taken: traffic steer completed at 09:32 PST for 80% of routes; full cutover pending capacity confirmation (estimating 20 minutes).
- Collected artifacts: perf_trace_1109.json (from customer), local engine logs, and a kernel selection dump. See link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/emeraldpay/perf-traces/1109
- Root cause hypothesis: quantization-induced change in attention kernel path combined with a hot-prefix cache miss pattern on a small set of high-cost prompts. The new kernel selection increases per-token stalls under the specific sequence-length distribution Emerald Pay has.

Reqs:
- Ops (Emily): please run the attached quick-export (we provided a small helper to tag failing request ids) and share 10 sample request ids experiencing 5xx so we can trace them through the runtime.
- Infra (Jonas): please prioritize a rollback if capacity projections show risk to SLA; otherwise complete 100% steer to v4beta. Also attach any gating logs showing kernel fallbacks.

Escalation: Emily mentioned CTO interest; if we cannot fully restore baseline within 1 hour we should prepare an exec slip and SLA remediation proposal. I will draft the postmortem template; Avery please coordinate communications.

Attachments referenced: sla-impact-summary.docx (short form for execs).

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Mike Tran <cto@emerald-pay.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, Emily Chen <ops@emerald-pay.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Degraded p99 + 5xx wave after v4alpha qprofile swap (urgent)

Marissa / Avery —

Appreciate the swift response. Emerald Pay's exec team reviewed the update. We have three asks before EOD:

1) Formal rollback confirmation and timestamp when our routes were back to v4beta. We saw improvements after the partial steer but need full rollback telemetry.
2) A summary of customer-visible impact (estimated % of requests affected, estimated downtime-equivalent for SLA computation) so our legal/procurement team can reconcile.

3) Our team is expecting a remediation credit request — please share Redwood's position and the SLA impact calculation.

We also want Redwood to keep v4alpha blocked for Emerald Pay until a joint verification run completes (we'll propose test prompts). We'll make time tomorrow for a deep-dive with your model ops and runtime engineers.

If you need a single exec contact here, loop me in and we'll coordinate with our CEO.

— Mike Tran
CTO, Emerald Pay
attachments: none
